HasTurnEndInHandEffect.maps_to: NOT PORTED -- DebtCard has no `has_turn_end_in_hand_effect` attribute (debt.py:23-33)
HasTurnEndInHandEffect.issue: `public override bool HasTurnEndInHandEffect => true` (Debt.cs:19) has no counterpart: the sim leaves the class default False (cards/base.py:63), so the end-of-turn hand pass never even asks Debt for an effect. This is the flag half of the same omission as the OnTurnEndInHand entry below and carries the same verdict.

OnTurnEndInHand.maps_to: NOT PORTED -- DebtCard has no `on_turn_end_in_hand` override (debt.py)
OnTurnEndInHand.issue: `Mathf.Min(DynamicVars.Gold.IntValue, Owner.Gold)` then `PlayerCmd.LoseGold(num, Owner)` (Debt.cs:26-30) is simply absent from the sim. The sim's own docstring (debt.py:20-21) justifies it with "The sim has no gold" -- THAT CLAIM IS FALSE. `RunState.gold` exists and `RunState.lose_gold` is implemented with the matching floor-at-zero semantics and a `PlayerCmd.LoseGold` citation (run.py:335-337); ported content spends and loses gold routinely (e.g. events/welcome_to_wongos.py buys with `lose_gold`). So Debt is a strictly weaker curse in the sim: in the game, holding it at end of turn costs up to 10 gold per turn, which compounds across a combat and changes what the player can afford at the next shop. LIVE -- Debt is a ported curse and gold is a ported, spendable resource. Note this is a rule-1 case: "the sim does not model it" is a dormant-or-live GAP, never a waiver, and here the resource IS modelled so it is live. RATIONALE CITES A THIRD FILE (rule 7): sts2_rl/run.py is not hashed by this record.

ctor.issue: CURSE / CURSE / NONE map exactly. The canonical energy cost is -1 in C# and 0 in the sim. `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers` returns early on `_base < 0` (CardEnergyCost.cs:100-103), so the game's unplayable card is immune to every cost modifier and keeps reporting -1; the sim runs a base of 0 through the full modifier chain (cards/base.py:222-232). `GetAmountToSpend()` clamps to Math.Max(0, ...) on both sides, so only what is READ diverges. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/ascenders_bane's ctor entry (rule 3). DORMANT: the ported cost readers all filter `> 0` or skip `<= 1` (relics/mummified_hand.py:25, potions.py:168, cards/event_cards.py:328), and events/infested_automaton.py:35 filters pool_card_ids(), which holds no curses or statuses.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: nothing -- there is no gold effect to hold the number (debt.py)
CanonicalVars.issue: `new GoldVar(10)` (Debt.cs:17) has no sim counterpart at all, which follows from the missing OnTurnEndInHand. Recorded separately because the number is also the card's printed value: `magic_number` returns None and the observation encoder sees no secondary number for Debt. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed DynamicVar with no `_`-attribute in `_init_vars`, so the sim's printed-number API reports the default and `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card wrongly for the policy. DORMANT for game fidelity (the dealt/applied number is identical), LIVE for the observation encoder.
